name: Protocol
summary: Records the method by which an observation was made, so that two results of the same phenomenon type obtained differently are not treated as interchangeable.

roles.name: Protocol
roles.summary: How the observation was obtained — which assay, which instrument, which procedure. Figure 3.10 hangs it off the phenomenon type at the knowledge level, and what it buys is comparability: two glucose readings taken by different methods have different reference ranges, so a trend line drawn through both is a clinical error that no arithmetic detects. Marking it says the comparison must ask.
